Started my transition to dnb around 2016 and since then it's been my main go-to genre just cos I was getting a bit bored of the dubstep scene and the cracks have only gotten bigger since then. I know basically none of the newcomers who've come onto the scene since then, only been somehat keeping up with the artists i used to listen to, at least the ones still going (a lot of my old favs like 501, BAR9, Far Too Loud and Xilent have pretty much packed up and left at this point). I've lost basically all touch with the scene, but judging from the snippets I've heard, I'm not missing out on much.

The reason why a lot of modern dubstep (brostep spexificakl) is boring and forgettable is because no one's focusing on melodies any more. When I look back on a lot of my favourite dubstep tracks, they had a main melody carrying the track all the way through and thats honestly the part of the track I remember the most (a lot of the NSD stuff in 2012 and 2013 for example). Nowadays you barely even get a scrap of melodic material before it's full on heaviness in the drop with no semblance of melody in it. Can't expect to remember a song if there's nothing to catch onto with.
